title: Wrap-up and the public record
summary: Kimery explains the archive; they talk about its public access and her coming to jazz through the Italian composer.

blocks.x: I think that’s a good place to wrap.

We should talk about the upcoming award, which is presented on April 4th. The project is National Endowment for the Arts, but also the Smithsonian Institution, and this is for the national record. This is your story that will be told.
Where is it told? People just can look it up? No one is going to get it, right? and online...
20 years from now, 30 years from now, 50 years from now, someone who wants to
You won’t have to worry about a good side any more.
I’ll have to worry about a good surgeon.
People who want to do some research on you and the Jazz Foundation will be able to access this interview, either the transcribed version, or they’ll be able to hear you.
Don’t you have to have a special library card to get that information? You mean anyone can...
No. We’re in public trust. This is the nation’s museum.
You’re in the same collection as Abbey Lincoln, and Sonny Rollins, and Quincy Jones.
What’s deep about it is that you weren’t involved in jazz at all until you took...
Until the affair with the Italian composer.
And then the JFA. I guess that’s a good revenge on him.
Oh, no revenge. I never have revenge with exes.
